literature.headline_zh: 人肠道病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期人肠道病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 肠道病毒 A71 感染外周细胞会增加细胞外囊泡的释放并丰富 microRNA-30 和 microRNA-34。这些囊泡抑制 Notch1 信号传导,损害内皮连接完整性,并增加血脑屏障通透性。临床上,患有严重肠道病毒 A71 相关手足口病的患者血清细胞外囊泡相关 microRNA-30 和 microRNA-34 升高。 [10.1038/s41467-026-79119-y]
本研究发现,多不饱和LCFA可以通过影响病毒生命周期的多个步骤来抑制肠道病毒的复制。LCFA的抗病毒活性并不依赖于其不饱和程度或诱导脂质过氧化的能力,而是与其构象显著相关。抑制中性脂质合成可促进LCFA重新定向到感染细胞的膜中,从而增强其抗病毒效果。 [10.1128/jvi.00902-26]
本研究发现,季节性EV-D68的传播早在2014年引起广泛关注的暴发之前就已经确立。此外,研究还表明,急性弛缓性脊髓炎病例负担与特定EV-D68谱系(谱系B)的传播动态有显著关联,而这种关联在谱系A和D中并未观察到。 [10.1038/s41467-026-78448-2]
疫苗 构建体预计具有抗原性、非过敏性、无毒性,并具有良好的理化特性。预计它还将覆盖全球 98.52% 的 HLA 人群。对接分析显示加权分数为-1134的排名最高的簇,C-ImmSim预测加强剂量后的继发性免疫应答。 [10.1186/s12866-026-05790-2]
患者出现贫血、血小板减少、急性肾损伤、血尿和蛋白尿,外周血涂片可见片状红细胞。补体评估显示 C3 和因子 I 浓度降低,可溶性 C5b-9 增加,并保留 ADAMTS13 活性。组织病理学分析证实皮肤血栓性微血管病伴微血管血栓形成。 [10.3389/fped.2026.1973640]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Enterovirus A71 infection of peripheral cells increases extracellular vesicle release and enriches microRNA-30 and microRNA-34. These vesicles suppress Notch1 signaling, impair endothelial junctional integrity, and increase blood-brain barrier permeability. [10.1038/s41467-026-79119-y]

The study found that polyunsaturated LCFAs can inhibit enterovirus replication by affecting multiple steps of the virus life cycle. The anti-viral activity of LCFAs was not dependent on their degree of unsaturation or capacity to induce lipid peroxidation but correlated with their conformation. [10.1128/jvi.00902-26]
The study found that seasonal EV-D68 transmission was well established long before the 2014 outbreak brought the virus to widespread attention. [10.1038/s41467-026-78448-2]
The prevalence of EV-A71 vaccine hesitancy among parents was 28.95%. [10.1186/s12889-026-29951-0]

The vaccine construct was predicted to be antigenic, non-allergenic, non-toxic, and to have favorable physicochemical properties. It was also predicted to cover 98.52% of the global HLA population. [10.1186/s12866-026-05790-2]

papers.title: Parental EV-A71 vaccine hesitancy amid shifting HFMD pathogens: a cross-sectional study in Guangzhou
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Following enterovirus A71 (EV‐A71) vaccine introduction, the hand foot mouth disease (HFMD) pathogen spectrum has shifted away from EV‐A71, prompting parental doubts about the vaccine’s continued relevance. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence and determinants of EV‐A71 vaccine hesitancy among parents in Guangzhou. Methods We surveyed parents of children ≤ 5 years at 10 community health centers in Guangzhou using stratified multi-stage sampling. Exploratory factor analysis identified latent variables, followed by structural equation modeling (SEM) to examine their direct and indirect effects on vaccine hesitancy. Logistic regression with cluster-robust standard errors was used to assess the effects of parental knowledge, attitude, and practice (KAP) and physician recommendation practices, specifically examining the cross-level interaction between physician recommendation enthusiasm and parental vaccine confidence. Results The prevalence of EV-A71 vaccine hesitancy among parents was 28.95%. Mothers (OR: 0.46[0.28, 0.76]) and parents with a college degree or associate degree (OR: 0.53[0.32, 0.86]) were less hesitant, whereas being a non‐healthcare worker (OR: 2.38[1.03, 5.55]) and having a child without a history of HFMD (OR: 3.45[1.31, 9.12]) were more hesitant. SEM indicated that vaccine confidence ( β = -0.39), service trust ( β = -0.17), and risk perception ( β = -0.17) exerted negative direct effects on vaccine hesitancy. Knowledge had no direct effect, its total indirect effect via the three mediators was significant( β = -0.45). Furthermore, the interaction between parental confidence and physician recommendation was marginally significant( β = 2.10, P = 0.08). Conclusion Knowledge reduces hesitancy mainly through confidence, trust, and risk perception, not directly. Communication and counseling addressing these attitudes may support informed parental decisions about voluntary, self-paid EV-A71 vaccination.

papers.title: Infection-specific long-chain fatty acid metabolism as a broad anti-enterovirus target.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Enteroviruses are arguably the most numerous group of viruses infecting humans. While most enterovirus infections are benign and self-resolving, their sheer number inevitably increases the chances of multiple complications. The diversity of enteroviruses means that the development of vaccines is only economically feasible against a select few, and no direct-acting or host-targeted anti-virals are approved to treat enteroviral infections, largely due to the rapid development of resistance against all experimental drugs. Here, we explored a universal property of enterovirus infection—a massive upregulation of phospholipid synthesis as a target for anti-viral interventions. The increased phospholipid synthesis consumes endogenously and exogenously derived long-chain fatty acids (LCFA). We demonstrate that polyunsaturated LCFAs can have a broad anti-enteroviral effect, affecting multiple steps of the virus life cycle. The anti-viral activity of LCFAs did not strictly depend on the degree of unsaturation or their capacity to induce lipid peroxidation, but significantly correlated with their conformation. This suggests that their incorporation into the phospholipid molecules makes the replication organelle membranes incapable of properly accommodating viral replication machinery. Accordingly, the inhibition of neutral lipid synthesis promoted LCFAs retargeting to the membranes in infected cells and increased their anti-viral potency. We show that this approach is effective against diverse enteroviruses in different cell types, including differentiated primary cells, and that attempts to establish viruses resistant to such treatment were unsuccessful. IMPORTANCE Humans are hosts to more than 300 distinct enteroviruses. Enterovirus infections can induce multiple short-term and long-term complications, including such serious conditions as paralysis, myocarditis, aseptic meningitis, and others. Yet, licensed vaccines are available only against poliovirus and enterovirus A71, and no specific anti-enterovirus drugs are approved for clinical practice. These viruses rapidly develop resistance to either virus- or host-acting experimental compounds. We explored a shared feature of enterovirus infection, a strong upregulation of phospholipid synthesis in infected cells, as a tool to control enterovirus replication. By altering the long-chain fatty acids composition available to infected cells, replication of diverse enteroviruses can be similarly suppressed, and the selection of resistant mutants was not successful. Thus, targeting infection-induced changes in cellular lipid metabolism, rather than individual viral or host factors, may offer a promising approach for controlling enterovirus infections. Humans are hosts to more than 300 distinct enteroviruses.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of effective anti-enterovirus treatments and vaccines, focusing on a universal property of enterovirus infection: the upregulation of phospholipid synthesis. This upregulation is a critical step in the virus life cycle and a potential target for anti-viral interventions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved exploring the effects of long-chain fatty acids (LCFAs) on enterovirus infection in various cell types, including primary cells, to identify a broad anti-enteroviral target.
analysis.methods: The researchers investigated the impact of LCFAs on enterovirus infection by altering the fatty acid composition available to infected cells and analyzing the effects on viral replication and lipid metabolism.
analysis.main_results: The study found that polyunsaturated LCFAs can inhibit enterovirus replication by affecting multiple steps of the virus life cycle. The anti-viral activity of LCFAs was not dependent on their degree of unsaturation or capacity to induce lipid peroxidation but correlated with their conformation. Inhibition of neutral lipid synthesis promoted LCFAs retargeting to the membranes in infected cells, increasing their anti-viral potency.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted their findings as demonstrating a novel approach to controlling enterovirus infections by targeting infection-induced changes in cellular lipid metabolism, which could be effective against diverse enteroviruses and resistant to viral resistance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest a promising approach for controlling enterovirus infections, which could lead to new treatments and reduce the burden of enterovirus-related complications.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the use of in vitro models and the need for further validation in vivo. The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on in vitro data and the lack of direct clinical application.

analysis.summary_en: This study explored the use of long-chain fatty acids as a broad anti-enteroviral target, demonstrating their effectiveness in inhibiting enterovirus replication across various cell types. The findings suggest a promising approach for controlling enterovirus infections, which could lead to new treatments and reduce the burden of enterovirus-related complications.

This upregulation is a critical step in the virus life cycle and a potential target for anti-viral interventions.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study involved exploring the effects of long-chain fatty acids (LCFAs) on enterovirus infection in various cell types, including primary cells, to identify a broad anti-enteroviral target.
elements_en.methods: The researchers investigated the impact of LCFAs on enterovirus infection by altering the fatty acid composition available to infected cells and analyzing the effects on viral replication and lipid metabolism.
elements_en.main_results: The study found that polyunsaturated LCFAs can inhibit enterovirus replication by affecting multiple steps of the virus life cycle. The anti-viral activity of LCFAs was not dependent on their degree of unsaturation or capacity to induce lipid peroxidation but correlated with their conformation. Inhibition of neutral lipid synthesis promoted LCFAs retargeting to the membranes in infected cells, increasing their anti-viral potency.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted their findings as demonstrating a novel approach to controlling enterovirus infections by targeting infection-induced changes in cellular lipid metabolism, which could be effective against diverse enteroviruses and resistant to viral resistance.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest a promising approach for controlling enterovirus infections, which could lead to new treatments and reduce the burden of enterovirus-related complications.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the use of in vitro models and the need for further validation in vivo. The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on in vitro data and the lack of direct clinical application.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在解决缺乏有效的抗肠道病毒治疗和疫苗的问题,聚焦于肠道病毒感染的一个普遍特性:磷脂合成的上调。这种上调是病毒生命周期中的关键步骤,也是抗病毒干预的潜在靶点。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及在多种细胞类型(包括原代细胞)中探索长链脂肪酸(LCFA)对肠道病毒感染的影响,以确定一种广泛的抗肠道病毒靶点。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员通过改变感染细胞可利用的脂肪酸组成,并分析其对病毒复制和脂质代谢的影响,来研究LCFA对肠道病毒感染的作用。
elements_zh.main_results: 本研究发现,多不饱和LCFA可以通过影响病毒生命周期的多个步骤来抑制肠道病毒的复制。LCFA的抗病毒活性并不依赖于其不饱和程度或诱导脂质过氧化的能力,而是与其构象显著相关。抑制中性脂质合成可促进LCFA重新定向到感染细胞的膜中,从而增强其抗病毒效果。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将他们的发现解释为展示了一种通过靶向感染诱导的细胞脂质代谢变化来控制肠道病毒感染的新方法,这种方法可能对多种肠道病毒有效,并且能够抵抗病毒的抗药性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,针对感染诱导的细胞脂质代谢变化进行干预可能为控制肠道病毒感染提供一种有前景的方法,这可能有助于开发新的治疗并减少与肠道病毒相关的并发症负担。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性包括使用体外模型以及需要进一步在体内验证。由于依赖体外数据且缺乏直接的临床应用,其证据强度中等。

papers.title_zh: 感染特异性长链脂肪酸代谢作为广泛抗肠道病毒靶点。
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Enteroviruses are arguably the most numerous group of viruses infecting humans. While most enterovirus infections are benign and self-resolving, their sheer number inevitably increases the chances of multiple complications. The diversity of enteroviruses means that the development of vaccines is only economically feasible against a select few, and no direct-acting or host-targeted anti-virals are approved to treat enteroviral infections, largely due to the rapid development of resistance against all experimental drugs. Here, we explored a universal property of enterovirus infection—a massive upregulation of phospholipid synthesis as a target for anti-viral interventions. The increased phospholipid synthesis consumes endogenously and exogenously derived long-chain fatty acids (LCFA). We demonstrate that polyunsaturated LCFAs can have a broad anti-enteroviral effect, affecting multiple steps of the virus life cycle. The anti-viral activity of LCFAs did not strictly depend on the degree of unsaturation or their capacity to induce lipid peroxidation, but significantly correlated with their conformation. This suggests that their incorporation into the phospholipid molecules makes the replication organelle membranes incapable of properly accommodating viral replication machinery. Accordingly, the inhibition of neutral lipid synthesis promoted LCFAs retargeting to the membranes in infected cells and increased their anti-viral potency. We show that this approach is effective against diverse enteroviruses in different cell types, including differentiated primary cells, and that attempts to establish viruses resistant to such treatment were unsuccessful. IMPORTANCE Humans are hosts to more than 300 distinct enteroviruses. Enterovirus infections can induce multiple short-term and long-term complications, including such serious conditions as paralysis, myocarditis, aseptic meningitis, and others. Yet, licensed vaccines are available only against poliovirus and enterovirus A71, and no specific anti-enterovirus drugs are approved for clinical practice. These viruses rapidly develop resistance to either virus- or host-acting experimental compounds. We explored a shared feature of enterovirus infection, a strong upregulation of phospholipid synthesis in infected cells, as a tool to control enterovirus replication. By altering the long-chain fatty acids composition available to infected cells, replication of diverse enteroviruses can be similarly suppressed, and the selection of resistant mutants was not successful. Thus, targeting infection-induced changes in cellular lipid metabolism, rather than individual viral or host factors, may offer a promising approach for controlling enterovirus infections. Humans are hosts to more than 300 distinct enteroviruses.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 肠道病毒是感染人类的病毒中最常见的类型。尽管大多数肠道病毒感染是良性的且可自愈,但它们的数量庞大不可避免地增加了多种并发症的风险。由于肠道病毒的多样性,开发针对特定少数病毒的疫苗在经济上仅具可行性,且目前尚无直接作用或针对宿主的抗病毒药物获批用于治疗肠道病毒感染,这主要是由于所有实验药物都迅速产生抗药性。在此,我们探索了肠道病毒感染的一个普遍特性——感染细胞中磷脂合成的显著上调,作为抗病毒干预的靶点。增加的磷脂合成消耗了内源性和外源性长链脂肪酸(LCFA)。我们证明,多不饱和LCFA可以对多种肠道病毒产生广泛的抗病毒效果,影响病毒生命周期的多个步骤。LCFA的抗病毒活性并不严格依赖于其不饱和程度或诱导脂质过氧化的能力,而是与其构象显著相关。这表明,它们被纳入磷脂分子后,会使复制细胞器膜无法适当地容纳病毒复制机器。因此,抑制中性脂质合成可促进LCFA重新定向到感染细胞的膜中,从而增强其抗病毒效果。我们展示了这种方法在不同细胞类型(包括分化后的原代细胞)中对多种肠道病毒均有效,并且尝试建立对这种治疗具有抗性的病毒均未成功。重要性 人类对超过300种不同的肠道病毒具有宿主。肠道病毒感染可引起多种短期和长期并发症,包括瘫痪、心肌炎、无菌性脑膜炎等严重情况。然而,目前仅针对脊髓灰质炎病毒和肠道病毒A71有批准的疫苗药物,且尚无专门针对肠道病毒的药物获批用于临床治疗。这些病毒对任何病毒作用或宿主作用的实验化合物都迅速产生抗药性。我们探索了肠道病毒感染的一个共同特征——感染细胞中磷脂合成的强烈上调,作为控制肠道病毒复制的工具。通过改变感染细胞可利用的长链脂肪酸组成,可以同样抑制多种肠道病毒的复制,且未能成功选择出抗性突变体。因此,针对感染诱导的细胞脂质代谢变化进行干预,而不是针对个别病毒或宿主因素,可能为控制肠道病毒感染提供一种有前景的方法。人类对超过300种不同的肠道病毒具有宿主。

papers.title: Clade-specific transmission dynamics of enterovirus D68 and their association with acute flaccid myelitis
papers.abstract: Abstract Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) is a common cause of mild respiratory illness in children but is also linked to acute flaccid myelitis (AFM), a rare and severe neurological condition which can result in permanent paralysis. Tracking EV-D68 transmission is difficult because symptoms overlap with other common childhood illnesses, making case reporting unreliable. As a result, the burden of EV-D68 transmission remains poorly understood, particularly prior to the first widely recognised outbreak in 2014. Phylodynamic approaches offer a powerful alternative to case-based surveillance, inferring epidemiological parameters directly from pathogen genetic sequences. Here we show, using a birth-death-sampling phylodynamic model applied to publicly available EV-D68 sequences from the 1990s to 2023 collected in Europe and North America, that seasonal EV-D68 transmission was well established long before the 2014 outbreak brought the virus to widespread attention. Furthermore, we show that AFM case burden is strongly associated with the transmission dynamics of a specific EV-D68 clade, clade B, an association not seen for clades A and D. These findings suggest that clade-specific biological differences drive AFM risk, with important implications for surveillance prioritisation and the timing of future burden of neurological disease.

Phylodynamic approaches offer a powerful alternative to case-based surveillance, inferring epidemiological parameters directly from pathogen genetic sequences. Here we show, using a birth-death-sampling phylodynamic model applied to publicly available EV-D68 sequences from the 1990s to 2023 collected in Europe and North America, that seasonal EV-D68 transmission was well established long before the 2014 outbreak brought the virus to widespread attention. Furthermore, we show that AFM case burden is strongly associated with the transmission dynamics of a specific EV-D68 clade, clade B, an association not seen for clades A and D. These findings suggest that clade-specific biological differences drive AFM risk, with important implications for surveillance prioritisation and the timing of future burden of neurological disease.

papers.title: Case Report: Atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome triggered by Rhinovirus/Enterovirus infection with cutaneous thrombotic microangiopathy requiring surgical management
papers.abstract: Atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS) represents a complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) characterized by microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and end-organ damage, most frequently affecting the kidneys. Although infection is a well-recognized precipitant, extensive skin involvement is uncommon. Here, we describe a 14-year-old boy who developed aHUS following Rhinovirus/Enterovirus infection. He was found to have anemia, thrombocytopenia, acute kidney injury, hematuria, and proteinuria, and peripheral smear examination demonstrated schistocytes. Complement evaluation showed reduced C3 and factor I concentrations, increased soluble C5b-9, and preserved ADAMTS13 activity. Investigations for Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli, systemic autoimmune disease, and alternative infectious etiologies were negative. Even with eculizumab, corticosteroids, therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE), and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), his condition progressed to petechiae, ecchymoses, hemorrhagic bullae, and necrotic lesions of the axilla, neck, and back. Since the necrotic areas failed to heal and were accompanied by continued platelet consumption and a heightened risk of infection, surgical debridement and wound closure were undertaken after the platelet count reached 81 × 10^9/L. Histopathologic analysis of the excised tissue confirmed cutaneous thrombotic microangiopathy with microvascular thrombosis. Following the procedure, platelet count, hemoglobin, and complement C3 returned to normal, and the wound healed without complication. At subsequent follow-up, the scars were supple and level, with no sensory deficit or functional limitation. This report expands the range of infectious triggers associated with aHUS and demonstrates that persistent necrotic cutaneous thrombotic microangiopathy may necessitate prompt surgical management in addition to complement inhibition and supportive treatment.

Although infection is a well-recognized precipitant, extensive skin involvement is uncommon. Here, we describe a 14-year-old boy who developed aHUS following Rhinovirus/Enterovirus infection. He was found to have anemia, thrombocytopenia, acute kidney injury, hematuria, and proteinuria, and peripheral smear examination demonstrated schistocytes. Complement evaluation showed reduced C3 and factor I concentrations, increased soluble C5b-9, and preserved ADAMTS13 activity. Investigations for Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli, systemic autoimmune disease, and alternative infectious etiologies were negative. Even with eculizumab, corticosteroids, therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE), and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), his condition progressed to petechiae, ecchymoses, hemorrhagic bullae, and necrotic lesions of the axilla, neck, and back. Since the necrotic areas failed to heal and were accompanied by continued platelet consumption and a heightened risk of infection, surgical debridement and wound closure were undertaken after the platelet count reached 81 × 10^9/L. Histopathologic analysis of the excised tissue confirmed cutaneous thrombotic microangiopathy with microvascular thrombosis. Following the procedure, platelet count, hemoglobin, and complement C3 returned to normal, and the wound healed without complication. At subsequent follow-up, the scars were supple and level, with no sensory deficit or functional limitation. This report expands the range of infectious triggers associated with aHUS and demonstrates that persistent necrotic cutaneous thrombotic microangiopathy may necessitate prompt surgical management in addition to complement inhibition and supportive treatment.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to report a case of atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS) triggered by Rhinovirus/Enterovirus infection, expanding the range of infectious triggers associated with aHUS. The background highlights the complement-mediated nature of aHUS and the rarity of extensive skin involvement.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A case report of a 14-year-old boy who developed aHUS following Rhinovirus/Enterovirus infection. The study was conducted to describe the clinical course and management of this rare condition.
analysis.methods: The patient was evaluated for aHUS through clinical examination, laboratory tests including complement evaluation, and histopathologic analysis of excised tissue. Treatment involved eculizumab, corticosteroids, therapeutic plasma exchange, and continuous renal replacement therapy.
analysis.main_results: The patient presented with anemia, thrombocytopenia, acute kidney injury, hematuria, and proteinuria, with schistocytes on peripheral smear. Complement evaluation showed reduced C3 and factor I concentrations, increased soluble C5b-9, and preserved ADAMTS13 activity. Histopathologic analysis confirmed cutaneous thrombotic microangiopathy with microvascular thrombosis.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The report expands the range of infectious triggers associated with aHUS and demonstrates that persistent necrotic cutaneous thrombotic microangiopathy may necessitate prompt surgical management in addition to complement inhibition and supportive treatment.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that Rhinovirus/Enterovirus infections can trigger aHUS and that surgical debridement may be necessary for persistent necrotic cutaneous involvement. This has implications for the management of aHUS cases with skin involvement.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a case report and thus limited by its small sample size and lack of generalizability. The patient's condition progressed despite treatment, highlighting the challenges in managing aHUS with persistent skin involvement.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 14-year-old boy who developed atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS) following Rhinovirus/Enterovirus infection. papers.abstract_zh: 非典型溶血性尿毒症综合征 (aHUS) 是一种补体介导的血栓性微血管病 (TMA),其特征为微血管病性溶血性贫血、血小板减少症和终末器官损伤,最常影响肾脏。尽管感染是公认的诱因,但广泛的皮肤受累并不常见。在这里,我们描述了一名 14 岁男孩在鼻病毒/肠道病毒感染后患上 aHUS。查出贫血、血小板减少、急性肾损伤、血尿、蛋白尿,外周血涂片检查提示裂细胞。补体评估显示 C3 和因子 I 浓度降低,可溶性 C5b-9 增加,并保留 ADAMTS13 活性。对产志贺毒素大肠杆菌、系统性自身免疫性疾病和其他感染病因的调查结果均为阴性。即使使用依库丽单抗、皮质类固醇、治疗性血浆置换 (TPE) 和连续肾脏替代疗法 (CRRT),他的病情仍进展为瘀点、瘀斑、出血性大疱以及腋窝、颈部和背部的坏死性病变。由于坏死部位无法愈合,血小板持续消耗,感染风险增加,待血小板计数达到81×10^9/L后,进行手术清创、闭合伤口。切除组织的组织病理学分析证实皮肤血栓性微血管病伴微血管血栓形成。手术后,血小板计数、血红蛋白和补体C3恢复正常,伤口愈合,无并发症。在随后的随访中,疤痕柔软且水平,没有感觉缺陷或功能限制。该报告扩大了与 aHUS 相关的感染触发因素的范围,并表明,除了补体抑制和支持性 治疗 之外,持续性坏死性皮肤血栓性微血管病可能还需要及时进行手术治疗。

papers.title: Beyond polio: advanced human in vitro models for studying non-polio enterovirus pathogenesis
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT While efforts to eradicate poliovirus are ongoing, non-polio enteroviruses (NPEV) continue to pose a substantial public health threat. NPEVs cause a wide range of diseases, from mild self-limiting infections to severe respiratory, neurological, and cardiac complications, with the highest burden occurring in children and immunocompromised populations. Recent advances in human stem cell-derived cultures, organoids, air-liquid interface systems, and assembloids have transformed the study of NPEV pathogenesis by providing physiologically relevant models that recapitulate human tissue architecture, cellular complexity, and host responses. In this review, we discuss how these advanced in vitro systems have enhanced our understanding of the determinants of viral tropism, including receptor usage, epithelial polarity, tissue-specific susceptibility, and viral genetic variation. We further highlight insights into serotype-dependent differences in innate immune responses, tissue injury, and dissemination mechanisms. Finally, we explore the potential of these models for antiviral discovery and personalized therapeutic development, emphasizing their value for advancing both fundamental and translational NPEV research.

papers.title_original: Beyond polio: advanced human in vitro models for studying non-polio enterovirus pathogenesis

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on non-polio human enteroviruses, particularly EV-A71, EV-D68, CV-A6, CV-A16, and echoviruses, and examines their pathogenesis through advanced human in vitro models. The central question is how these models have improved our understanding of viral tropism, immune responses, and dissemination mechanisms in these pathogens.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of recent advances in human stem cell-derived cultures, organoids, air-liquid interface systems, and assembloids. It discusses their application in studying NPEV pathogenesis, including receptor usage, epithelial polarity, tissue-specific susceptibility, and genetic variation. The review does not report on meta-analysis or pooled estimates but provides a general overview of the methodologies used.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that recent in vitro models have significantly enhanced the study of NPEV pathogenesis by replicating human tissue architecture, cellular complexity, and host responses. These models have provided insights into serotype-dependent differences in innate immune responses, tissue injury, and dissemination mechanisms, which are critical for understanding the disease processes of these viruses.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while these models have advanced our understanding, there are still unresolved questions regarding the precise mechanisms of viral tropism and the role of genetic variation in disease severity. Additionally, the review identifies gaps in the understanding of how these models can be optimized for personalized therapeutic development.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that further research should focus on refining these in vitro models to better reflect human physiology and disease progression. It also emphasizes the potential of these models for antiviral discovery and personalized therapeutic development, which could lead to more effective treatments and prevention strategies for NPEVs.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the use of advanced human in vitro models in studying non-polio enteroviruses (NPEVs), including EV-A71, EV-D68, CV-A6, CV-A16, and echoviruses. It highlights how these models have transformed the understanding of viral tropism, immune responses, and dissemination mechanisms. The review also identifies gaps in knowledge and suggests future research directions for improving antiviral discovery and personalized therapeutic development. The findings underscore the importance of these models in advancing both fundamental and translational research on NPEVs.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注非脊髓灰质炎 人肠道病毒,特别是 EV-A71、EV-D68、CV-A6、CV-A16 和埃可病毒,并通过先进的人体体外模型检查其 发病机制。核心问题是这些模型如何提高我们对病毒趋向性、免疫应答 和这些病原体传播机制的理解。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评论是对人类干细胞衍生培养物、类器官、气液界面系统和组合体方面最新进展的叙述性综合。它讨论了它们在研究 NPEV 发病机制 中的应用,包括受体使用、上皮极性、组织特异性易感性和遗传变异。该综述不报告荟萃分析或汇总估计,而是提供所用方法的总体概述。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述强调,最近的体外模型通过复制人体组织结构、细胞复杂性和 宿主 反应,显着增强了 NPEV 发病机制 的研究。这些模型提供了对先天 免疫应答 血清型依赖性差异、组织损伤和传播机制的见解,这对于了解这些病毒的疾病过程至关重要。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该评论指出,虽然这些模型增进了我们的理解,但关于病毒趋向性的精确机制以及遗传变异在疾病严重程度中的作用,仍然存在未解决的问题。此外,该评论还指出了对如何优化这些模型以实现个性化治疗开发的理解上的差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该评论表明,进一步的研究应集中于完善这些体外模型,以更好地反映人类生理学和疾病进展。它还强调了这些模型在 抗病毒药物 发现和个性化治疗开发方面的潜力,这可能会导致更有效的 治疗 和 NPEV 预防策略。

papers.full_text: Abstract Enterovirus A71 infection can cause hand, foot, and mouth disease to occasionally develop the severe neurological complications, but how peripheral Enterovirus A71 infection affects the blood-brain barrier remains incompletely understood. Here, we show that Enterovirus A71 infection of peripheral susceptible cells increases the release of extracellular vesicles and promotes the enrichment of microRNA-30 and microRNA-34 within these vesicles. The extracellular vesicle-associated microRNAs suppress Notch1 signaling in human brain microvascular endothelial cells, impair endothelial junctional integrity, and increase blood-brain barrier permeability. Activation of Notch1 signaling restores barrier integrity and reduces viral neuroinvasion in neonatal mice. Clinically, serum extracellular vesicle-associated microRNA-30 and microRNA-34 are elevated in patients with severe Enterovirus A71-associated hand, foot, and mouth disease. Together, our findings identify circulating extracellular vesicles as mediators linking peripheral Enterovirus A71 infection to blood-brain barrier dysfunction and suggest that the microRNA-30/34–Notch1 axis contributes to neurological disease progression during severe Enterovirus A71 infection. analysis.research_question_and_background: Enterovirus A71 infection can cause hand, foot, and mouth disease to occasionally develop severe neurological complications, but how peripheral Enterovirus A71 infection affects the blood-brain barrier remains incompletely understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study demonstrates that Enterovirus A71 infection of peripheral susceptible cells increases the release of extracellular vesicles and promotes the enrichment of microRNA-30 and microRNA-34 within these vesicles. The extracellular vesicle-associated microRNAs suppress Notch1 signaling in human brain microvascular endothelial cells, impair endothelial junctional integrity, and increase blood-brain barrier permeability.
analysis.methods: The study used human brain microvascular endothelial cells to examine the effects of extracellular vesicles from Enterovirus A71-infected peripheral cells on Notch1 signaling. It also included clinical data showing elevated serum extracellular vesicle-associated microRNA-30 and microRNA-34 in patients with severe Enterovirus A71-associated hand, foot, and mouth disease.
analysis.main_results: Enterovirus A71 infection of peripheral cells increases extracellular vesicle release and enriches microRNA-30 and microRNA-34. These vesicles suppress Notch1 signaling, impair endothelial junctional integrity, and increase blood-brain barrier permeability. Clinically, serum extracellular vesicle-associated microRNA-30 and microRNA-34 are elevated in patients with severe Enterovirus A71-associated hand, foot, and mouth disease.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings identify circulating extracellular vesicles as mediators linking peripheral Enterovirus A71 infection to blood-brain barrier dysfunction and suggest that the microRNA-30/34–Notch1 axis contributes to neurological disease progression during severe Enterovirus A71 infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide insights into the mechanisms of neurological complications in Enterovirus A71 infection and suggest potential targets for therapeutic interventions to prevent viral neuroinvasion.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on in vitro and animal models, and the clinical data are observational. However, the evidence is strong and directly supports the proposed mechanism of Enterovirus A71-induced blood-brain barrier dysfunction.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how Enterovirus A71 infection affects the blood-brain barrier. It shows that peripheral Enterovirus A71 infection increases extracellular vesicle release and enriches microRNA-30 and microRNA-34, which suppress Notch1 signaling in brain endothelial cells, impairing junctional integrity and increasing permeability. Clinically, elevated levels of these microRNAs in serum are observed in patients with severe Enterovirus A71-associated hand, foot, and mouth disease. The findings suggest that circulating extracellular vesicles mediate the link between peripheral infection and neurological complications, highlighting the microRNA-30/34–Notch1 axis as a potential therapeutic target. While the study uses in vitro and animal models, the evidence is strong and directly supports the proposed mechanism of viral neuroinvasion.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 肠道病毒 A71 感染可导致手足口病,偶尔会出现严重的神经系统并发症,但外周肠道病毒 A71 感染如何影响血脑屏障仍不完全清楚。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 研究表明,肠道病毒 A71 感染外周易感细胞会增加细胞外囊泡的释放,并促进这些囊泡内 microRNA-30 和 microRNA-34 的富集。细胞外囊泡相关的 microRNA 抑制人脑微血管内皮细胞中的 Notch1 信号传导,损害内皮连接完整性,并增加血脑屏障的通透性。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用人脑微血管内皮细胞来检查肠道病毒 A71 感染的外周细胞的细胞外囊泡对 Notch1 信号传导的影响。它还包括临床数据,显示患有严重肠道病毒 A71 相关手足口病的患者血清细胞外囊泡相关 microRNA-30 和 microRNA-34 升高。
elements_zh.main_results: 肠道病毒 A71 感染外周细胞会增加细胞外囊泡的释放并丰富 microRNA-30 和 microRNA-34。这些囊泡抑制 Notch1 信号传导,损害内皮连接完整性,并增加血脑屏障通透性。临床上,患有严重肠道病毒 A71 相关手足口病的患者血清细胞外囊泡相关 microRNA-30 和 microRNA-34 升高。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果确定循环细胞外囊泡是外周肠道病毒 A71 感染与血脑屏障功能障碍之间的介导物,并表明 microRNA-30/34-Notch1 轴有助于严重肠道病毒 A71 感染期间的神经系统疾病进展。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了对肠道病毒 A71 感染神经系统并发症机制的见解,并提出了预防病毒神经侵袭的治疗干预的潜在目标。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究由于依赖体外和动物模型而受到限制,并且临床数据是观察性的。然而,证据确凿,直接支持肠道病毒 A71 诱导血脑屏障功能障碍的机制。

papers.title: Comprehensive immunoinformatics analysis and chimeric multi-epitope vaccine design targeting VP1 capsid protein of poliovirus type 3
papers.abstract: Poliomyelitis is caused by poliovirus, a member of the genus Enterovirus in the family Picornaviridae. Oral and inactivated poliovirus vaccines have substantially reduced disease worldwide; however, limitations include incomplete intestinal immunity after inactivated vaccine and the rare emergence of vaccine-derived strains after oral vaccine, supporting investigation of non-replicating vaccine platforms. Poliomyelitis is classified into three distinct forms: mild disease (abortive poliomyelitis), paralytic poliomyelitis, and aseptic meningitis (nonparalytic poliomyelitis). Severe neurological complications, including irreversible paralysis, have affected thousands of individuals worldwide. Polio is prevented via vaccination, namely with the inactivated and attenuated oral polio vaccine. Although existing vaccines have driven global eradication, IPV provides limited intestinal mucosal immunity, and OPV can rarely be associated with vaccine-derived poliovirus, motivating evaluation of a non-replicating vaccine platform.Abstruct. This study used immunoinformatics to design and preliminarily evaluate a chimeric multi-epitope vaccine candidate targeting the VPI capsid protein of poliovirus type 3. The VPI sequence (NCB accession number ABG78772.1) was used for linear B-cell, MHC-class I, and MHC-class II epitope prediction and safty filtering. Selected epitopes were joined with defined linkers and an N-terminal human beta-defensin adjuvant. The resulting construct was evaluated for physicochemical properties, structural quality, predicted HLA population coverage, rigid-body docking with TLR3, normal-mode behaviour, and simulated immune responses. Codon adaptation and in silico cloning were also performed to evaluate the potential expression feasibility of the vaccine construct. Four B-cell epitopes, twenty-six cytotoxic T-lymphocyte epitopes, twenty helper T-lymphocyte epitopes, including EAAAK, GPGPG, and AAY linkers and β-defensin, were assembled into a 569-amino-acid construct. The construct was predicted to be antigenic, non-allergenic, non-toxic, and to show favourable physicochemical properties, including hydrophilic characteristics. Combined MCH-I and MCH-II epitopes predicted global HLA population coverage of 98.52%. CLustPro identified a top-ranked docked cluster with a weighted score of -1134; this score ranks models within the docking run and is not a binding free energy or dissociation constant. C-ImmSim predicted secondary humoral and cellular responses after booster doses, while codon analysis suggested compatibility with expression in Escherichia coli. Conclusion: The computational findings support the construct as a preliminary candidate for further study. They do not establish immunogenicity, safety, protective efficacy, receptor activation, or expression, all of which require experimental validation and in vitro and in vivo testing before biological conclusions can be drawn.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a computational design of a chimeric multi-epitope vaccine targeting the VP1 capsid protein of poliovirus type 3. The researchers used immunoinformatics to predict epitopes and assemble them into a 569-amino-acid construct with linkers and an adjuvant. The construct was evaluated for physicochemical properties, docking with TLR3, and simulated immune responses. The results indicate that the vaccine is predicted to be antigenic, non-allergenic, non-toxic, and to have favorable properties, with 98.52% HLA population coverage. The findings may inform the development of non-replicating vaccine platforms for poliovirus type 3, addressing limitations of current vaccines. The evidence is moderate due to reliance on in silico methods and lack of experimental data.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在设计和评估针对 3 型脊髓灰质炎病毒 VP1 衣壳蛋白的嵌合多表位 疫苗,因为现有的 疫苗 在肠道免疫方面存在局限性,并且 疫苗 衍生菌株的风险罕见。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是一项计算分析,旨在设计针对 3 型脊髓灰质炎病毒的 疫苗 候选药物,没有提及特定人群或环境。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员利用免疫信息学从 3 型脊髓灰质炎病毒的 VP1 序列中预测 B 细胞、MHC I 类和 MHC II 类表位,并将它们组装成带有接头和佐剂的 疫苗 结构。他们还评估了理化特性、与 TLR3、免疫应答 的对接以及表达可行性。
elements_zh.main_results: 疫苗 构建体预计具有抗原性、非过敏性、无毒性,并具有良好的理化特性。预计它还将覆盖全球 98.52% 的 HLA 人群。对接分析显示加权分数为-1134的排名最高的簇,C-ImmSim预测加强剂量后的继发性免疫应答。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 计算结果表明,疫苗 构建体有潜力作为进一步研究的初步候选者,尽管它们没有证实免疫原性、安全性或有效性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能为针对 3 型脊髓灰质炎病毒的非复制 疫苗 平台的开发提供信息,从而有可能解决当前 疫苗 的局限性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于计算预测,并未建立需要实验验证的免疫原性、安全性或保护功效。证据是温和的,因为它依赖于计算机方法。

papers.abstract_zh: 脊髓灰质炎是由脊髓灰质炎病毒引起的,脊髓灰质炎病毒是小核糖核酸病毒科肠道病毒属的成员。口服灭活脊髓灰质炎病毒 疫苗 已大大减少了全世界的疾病;然而,局限性包括灭活 疫苗 后肠道免疫不完整,以及口服 疫苗 后很少出现 疫苗 衍生菌株,支持非复制 疫苗 平台的研究。脊髓灰质炎分为三种不同的形式:轻度疾病(流产性脊髓灰质炎)、麻痹性脊髓灰质炎和无菌性脑膜炎(非麻痹性脊髓灰质炎)。严重的神经系统并发症,包括不可逆性瘫痪,已经影响了全世界数千人。脊髓灰质炎是通过 疫苗接种 预防的,即使用灭活和减毒的口服脊髓灰质炎 疫苗。尽管现有的 疫苗 已推动全球根除,但 IPV 提供的肠粘膜免疫力有限,并且 OPV 很少与 疫苗 衍生的脊髓灰质炎病毒相关,从而激发了对非复制 疫苗 平台的评估。本研究利用免疫信息学设计并初步评估了针对3型脊髓灰质炎病毒VPI衣壳蛋白的嵌合多表位候选物疫苗。VPI序列(NCB登录号ABG78772.1)用于线性B细胞、MHC I类和MHC II类表位预测和安全过滤。选定的表位与确定的接头和 N 末端人 β-防御素佐剂连接。对所得构建体的理化特性、结构质量、预测的 HLA 群体覆盖率、与 TLR3 的刚体对接、正常模式行为和模拟的 免疫应答 进行了评估。还进行了密码子适应和计算机克隆以评估 疫苗 构建体的潜在表达可行性。将 4 个 B 细胞表位、26 个细胞毒性 T 淋巴细胞表位、20 个辅助 T 淋巴细胞表位(包括 EAAAK、GPPGG、AAY 连接子和 β-防御素)组装成 569 个氨基酸的构建体。该构建体预计具有抗原性、非过敏性、无毒性,并显示出良好的理化特性,包括亲水特性。MCH-I 和 MCH-II 组合表位预测全球 HLA 人群覆盖率为 98.52%。CLustPro 确定了一个排名靠前的对接簇,加权得分为 -1134;该分数对对接运行中的模型进行排名,并且不是结合自由能或解离常数。C-ImmSim 预测了加强剂量后的继发性体液和细胞反应,而密码子分析表明与大肠杆菌中的表达相容。结论:计算结果支持该结构作为进一步研究的初步候选者。它们没有确定免疫原性、安全性、保护功效、受体激活或表达,所有这些都需要实验验证以及体外和体内测试才能得出生物学结论。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在设计和评估针对 3 型脊髓灰质炎病毒 VP1 衣壳蛋白的嵌合多表位 疫苗,因为现有的 疫苗 在肠道免疫方面存在局限性,并且 疫苗 衍生菌株的风险罕见。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是一项计算分析,旨在设计针对 3 型脊髓灰质炎病毒的 疫苗 候选药物,没有提及特定人群或环境。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员利用免疫信息学从 3 型脊髓灰质炎病毒的 VP1 序列中预测 B 细胞、MHC I 类和 MHC II 类表位,并将它们组装成带有接头和佐剂的 疫苗 结构。他们还评估了理化特性、与 TLR3、免疫应答 的对接以及表达可行性。
analysis_zh.main_results: 疫苗 构建体预计具有抗原性、非过敏性、无毒性,并具有良好的理化特性。预计它还将覆盖全球 98.52% 的 HLA 人群。对接分析显示加权分数为-1134的排名最高的簇,C-ImmSim预测加强剂量后的继发性免疫应答。

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可能为针对 3 型脊髓灰质炎病毒的非复制 疫苗 平台的开发提供信息,从而有可能解决当前 疫苗 的局限性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于计算预测,并未建立需要实验验证的免疫原性、安全性或保护功效。证据是温和的,因为它依赖于计算机方法。

papers.title: Reporter Virus-Based High-Throughput Screening Identifies LM-10 as a Novel Inhibitor Targeting KRM1 for Coxsackievirus A10 Blockade
papers.abstract: Enteroviruses causing hand, foot, and mouth disease, including currently circulating Coxsackievirus A10 (CVA10) and Coxsackievirus A6 (CVA6), rely on KREMEN1 (KRM1) for cell entry, making the virus–KRM1 interface a potential target for antiviral intervention. We screened GLMarNP, an in-house library of about 3000 natural products and derivatives. Candidates targeting the KRM1 ectodomain were selected by blind docking, drug-likeness assessment, and scaffold diversity analysis. To enable high-throughput antiviral screening, we inserted eGFP into a full-length infectious CVA10 cDNA clone to generate a reporter virus designated eGFP-A10. The virus was rescued in HEK293T cells and produced robust fluorescence in RD cells over serial passages. Among 29 candidate compounds, LM-10 showed the strongest antiviral activity and exhibited low cytotoxicity. Mechanistically, LM-10 bound KRM1 and acted early in the viral life cycle. Molecular docking suggested that LM-10 binds the KR domain at a site overlapping the VP2 EF-loop contact region. KRM1 also acts as a DKK1 receptor to regulate Wnt/β-catenin signaling. LM-10 did not significantly affect this pathway in the TOP-GFP reporter assay or in transgenic zebrafish embryos. These findings establish a practical CVA10 reporter-virus platform and support steric blockade of the receptor interface as a potential antiviral strategy.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify novel inhibitors targeting the KRM1 receptor for Coxsackievirus A10 (CVA10) blockage, addressing the need for antiviral intervention against enteroviruses causing hand, foot, and mouth disease.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A high-throughput screening of 3000 natural products and derivatives was conducted using a reporter virus-based platform in HEK293T and RD cells.
analysis_en.methods: Candidates were selected through blind docking, drug-likeness assessment, and scaffold diversity analysis. The reporter virus eGFP-A10 was generated by inserting eGFP into a full-length infectious CVA10 cDNA clone.
analysis_en.main_results: Among 29 candidate compounds, LM-10 showed the strongest antiviral activity and low cytotoxicity. LM-10 bound KRM1 and acted early in the viral life cycle.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings establish a practical CVA10 reporter-virus platform and support steric blockade of the receptor interface as a potential antiviral strategy.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results could inform the development of antiviral treatments for CVA10 and similar enteroviruses, contributing to the management of hand, foot, and mouth disease.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the need for further validation of LM-10's efficacy and safety in vivo and the potential for off-target effects on Wnt/β-catenin signaling.

papers.title_zh: 基于报告病毒的高通量筛选将 LM-10 确定为一种针对柯萨奇病毒 A10 阻断的 KRM1 新型抑制剂
papers.source_body_en: Enteroviruses causing hand, foot, and mouth disease, including currently circulating Coxsackievirus A10 (CVA10) and Coxsackievirus A6 (CVA6), rely on KREMEN1 (KRM1) for cell entry, making the virus–KRM1 interface a potential target for antiviral intervention. We screened GLMarNP, an in-house library of about 3000 natural products and derivatives. Candidates targeting the KRM1 ectodomain were selected by blind docking, drug-likeness assessment, and scaffold diversity analysis. To enable high-throughput antiviral screening, we inserted eGFP into a full-length infectious CVA10 cDNA clone to generate a reporter virus designated eGFP-A10. The virus was rescued in HEK293T cells and produced robust fluorescence in RD cells over serial passages. Among 29 candidate compounds, LM-10 showed the strongest antiviral activity and exhibited low cytotoxicity. Mechanistically, LM-10 bound KRM1 and acted early in the viral life cycle. Molecular docking suggested that LM-10 binds the KR domain at a site overlapping the VP2 EF-loop contact region. KRM1 also acts as a DKK1 receptor to regulate Wnt/β-catenin signaling. LM-10 did not significantly affect this pathway in the TOP-GFP reporter assay or in transgenic zebrafish embryos. These findings establish a practical CVA10 reporter-virus platform and support steric blockade of the receptor interface as a potential antiviral strategy.

papers.title: Ambient air pollution and meteorological factors associated with hand, foot, and mouth disease risk in Shenzhen, China: a time-series study

source_records.title: Ambient air pollution and meteorological factors associated with hand, foot, and mouth disease risk in Shenzhen, China: a time-series study
Ambient air pollution and meteorological factors associated with hand, foot, and mouth disease risk in Shenzhen, China: a time-series study

papers.priority_tier_reason: 补充性记录、预印本或证据完整度有限
papers.full_text: AbstractBackgroundIn China, hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) persists as a prevalent infectious disease with high transmissibility. Nevertheless, the link between environmental determinants and HFMD incidence has not been fully elucidated. The study assessed associations between air pollution, meteorological conditions, and HFMD incidence in Shenzhen, China, while also evaluating shifts in these associations before and after the Enterovirus 71 vaccine and during the COVID-19 epidemic.MethodsDaily data on HFMD cases, air pollutants (such as PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NO2, CO, and O3), and meteorological variables (including mean temperature, relative humidity, atmospheric pressure, and wind speed) were collected for the period from 2013 to 2022. Associations were assessed using distributed lag non-linear models (DLNM), accounting for immediate and delayed effects.ResultsSpearman correlation analysis showed that HFMD was positively correlated with SO2, mean temperature, relative humidity, and wind speed, and negatively with PM2.5, PM10, NO2, CO, and atmospheric pressure. DLNM models revealed that SO2 and CO both elevated cumulative risk at extremely high concentrations, with SO2 showing delayed effects. However, SO2 unexpectedly displayed protective effects in single-lag analysis. NO2 exhibited a U-shaped risk at extreme concentrations despite an overall decreasing trend. O3 showed dual peaks, with protective effects at extremely high concentrations after lag 1. PM2.5 and PM10 showed risk peaks at low concentrations but protective effects at extremely high concentrations. Temperature exhibited a dual-peak risk pattern at extremely low and extremely high temperatures, with extreme heat producing sustained effects and extreme cold shorter-lived risk. HFMD risk increased under conditions of extremely high humidity. In general, the risk associated with atmospheric pressure rose as pressure levels increased, and asymmetric lagged effects were observed at both low- and high-concentration extremes. Extremely high wind speed causing short-term harm and extremely low wind speed leading to delayed cumulative risk.ConclusionMeteorological factors exhibit more consistent associations than air pollutants. Mean temperature showed a dual-peak distribution with persistent effects from high temperatures, while atmospheric pressure presented long-lasting impacts of low pressure. There is a positive correlation between relative humidity and the incidence of HFMD. Air pollutants showed inconsistent associations with HFMD. These findings support targeted public health interventions for meteorological factors.Keywords: air pollution, DLNM, effect, HFMD, meteorological variables MethodsResearch area descriptionShenzhen, situated in the southern part of Guangdong Province, is a coastal metropolis sharing its border with Hong Kong and Macao. The city extends over 1,997 square kilometers and falls within the subtropical monsoon climate zone, experiencing an average annual temperature of nearly 23 °C. Over the 2013–2022 study period, Shenzhen’s annual permanent resident population stood between 12.57 million and 17.66 million, recording an average population of around 15.75 million.1 Geographically, Shenzhen lies within the coordinates 113.43°–114.38° E and 22.24°–22.52° N.2Data collectionDaily reported cases of HFMD covering the period 2013 to 2022 were collected from the infectious disease surveillance networks of Shenzhen Center for Disease Control and Prevention. Daily data spanning the same period, which included daily concentrations of air pollutants (PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NO2, CO, and O3) as well as meteorological conditions (mean temperature, relative humidity, atmospheric pressure, and wind speed), were acquired from Shenzhen Ecological Environment Monitoring Center Station and Meteorological Bureau of Shenzhen Municipality.3Statistical analysesDescriptive statistics summarized HFMD and environmental variables. To evaluate the associations between HFMD incidence and air pollution as well as meteorological factors, Spearman correlation analysis was conducted. The Spearman correlation coefficient was calculated as:rs=1−6∑i=1ndi2n(n2−1)Where di represents the difference between the ranks of paired observations for the i-th pair, and n is the number of observations. The Spearman coefficient ranges from −1 to +1, with positive values indicating a positive monotonic association and negative values indicating an inverse association. Statistical significance was defined as a two-sided p-value < 0.05.In line with earlier research, a quasi-Poisson regression framework incorporating distributed lag nonlinear models (DLNM) was used to examine the associations between air pollutants and meteorological conditions on HFMD occurrence, taking into account data distribution characteristics and inter-variable relationships. The model is specified as follows:log[E(Yt)]=α+cb(X,df=3,lag=21)+ns(Time,df=6/year)+Σns(Xi,df=3)+βDOWt+γHOLIDAYt+δVACt+εCOVtWhere α represents the intercept, and Yt is the number of HFMD cases observed on day t. The term cb(·) denotes the cross-basis function constructed with 3 df for the exposure dimension (natural cubic splines with knots placed at the 33rd and 67th percentiles) and 3 df for the lag dimension (natural cubic splines), with a maximum lag of 21 days. Each of the 10 environmental variables — PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NO2, CO, O3, mean temperature, relative humidity, atmospheric pressure, and wind speed — was separately examined as the primary exposure.For each model, natural cubic spline functions ns(·) with 3 df were applied to the remaining environmental variables (Xi) to adjust for their potential confounding effects. Given the high collinearity between PM2.5 and PM10 [Spearman ρ > 0.85; variance inflation factor (VIF) > 5; Supplementary Table S4], these two particulate matter fractions were not included simultaneously in any model. Specifically, when a meteorological variable (temperature, relative humidity, atmospheric pressure, or wind speed) served as the primary exposure, the covariates comprised the remaining meteorological variables together with CO, SO2, NO2, O3, and PM2.5 (PM10 excluded). When CO, SO2, NO2, or O3 served as the primary exposure, the covariates comprised the other three gaseous pollutants, all four meteorological variables, and PM2.5 (PM10 excluded). When PM2.5 or PM10 served as the primary exposure, the covariates comprised all four meteorological variables and the four gaseous pollutants (CO, SO2, NO2, O3), with the alternate particulate matter fraction excluded.The Time variable was specified with 6 df per year to capture long-term temporal trends and seasonal patterns, selected based on the quasi-Akaike information criterion (QAIC) (Supplementary Table S1). DOW and HOLIDAY denote the effects of the day of the week and public holidays. VAC and COV indicate whether the date fell within the EV71 vaccination or COVID-19 prevention period. The maximum lag of 21 days was selected based on QAIC comparison across 7, 14, and 21 days (Supplementary Table S2), and is consistent with the incubation period of enteroviruses and previous HFMD time-series studies (24). Knot placement at the 33rd and 67th percentiles was selected based on QAIC comparison with alternative strategies (Supplementary Table S3). As a sensitivity analysis to evaluate the potential impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, we repeated analyses excluding the pandemic period (2020–2022). Cumulative RRs at the 95th percentile were compared between the full-period (2013–2022) and pre-pandemic (2013–2019) datasets (Supplementary Table S5). We considered an association stable if both its direction and statistical significance remained consistent across the two datasets; associations that changed in direction or significance upon exclusion of the pandemic period were deemed sensitive to the inclusion of the pandemic period and are interpreted with caution throughout.Cumulative effects of environmental exposure variables on HFMD risk were measured for lags 0–21 days, using the meadian (50th) of each variable as a reference (Table 1). The effects of extreme exposures were expressed as relative risks (RRs), comparing the 5th and 95th percentiles to the median.Table 1Descriptive study of HFMD and environmental factors.VariablesMean ± SDMin25th50th75thMaxNumber of cases/day130 ± 14401777204885PM2.5 (μg/m3)26.34 ± 17.232.3313.7322.5534.86136.52PM10 (μg/m3)44.1 ± 24.883.2026.0438.1856.28179.77SO2 (μg/m3)7.73 ± 3.553.095.536.808.8256.03NO2 (μg/m3)32.06 ± 15.874.4021.2528.8938.77139.53CO (mg/m3)0.78 ± 0.260.390.570.710.901.92O3 (μg/m3)102.72 ± 45.7519.1866.7094.62128.38316.27Mean temperature(。C)23.62 ± 5.343.519.624.7528.233Atmospheric pressure (hPa)1005.63 ± 6.34983.11000.81005.61010.51027.3Relative humidity (%)75.41 ± 12.6819707884100Wind speed (m/s)1.83 ± 0.770.31.31.72.26.1To evaluate the potential influence of residual autocorrelation on our estimates, we performed the following two-step sensitivity analysis. First, the Pearson residuals of each main DLNM model were extracted, and residual autocorrelation was assessed diagnostically using the autocorrelation function (ACF) and the Ljung–Box test at lags of 10 and 20 days (Supplementary Table S6; Supplementary Figure S1). Second, to explicitly adjust for the first-order residual autocorrelation identified in the first step, we re-fitted each model including the first-order lagged Pearson residual as an additional covariate (hereinafter the AR(1)-adjusted model). The cumulative effect estimates of the AR(1)-adjusted models were then compared with those of the main models across all 60 exposure–percentile combinations (Supplementary Table S7). All analyses were performed using R software (version 4.4.2) with the dlnm package. Supplementary materialThe Supplementary material for this article can be found online at: https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fpubh.2026.1920424/full#supplementary-material Supplementary Materials ResultsCharacterization of research dataOver the decade spanning 2013 to 2022, there were 473,695 reported HFMD cases in Shenzhen (283,519 males, 190,176 females, annual mean: 47,370 cases). Table 1 and Figure 1 summarize case counts and environmental data. Figure 2 illustrates monthly HFMD case distribution, with cases peaking from May to October (the hot season).Figure 1Time series of meteorological and environmental pollution factors and number of HFMD cases.Multi-panel line graph displaying time series data from 2013 to 2023 for PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NO2, CO, O3, mean temperature, wind speed, atmospheric pressure, relative humidity, and case counts, highlighting annual and seasonal trends for each variable.Figure 2The monthly distribution of HFMD cases.Line chart depicting monthly hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) cases from 2013 to 2022, shows peak incidence between May and July, with the highest spike in 2019, followed by sharp declines.Correlation analysisAs demonstrated by the Spearman correlation analysis (Table 2), HFMD cases were significantly positively correlated with SO2, mean temperature, relative humidity, and wind speed, while negative correlations were identified with PM2.5, PM10, NO2, CO, and atmospheric pressure. The strongest correlation was observed for mean temperature (r = 0.61), followed by atmospheric pressure which had a correlation of r = −0.57. In the multivariate model, PM2.5 and PM10 cannot be added to the model at the same time, which is attributable to their extremely high correlation coefficient (r = 0.96).Table 2Correlation analysis of environmental factors and HFMD cases.VariablesHFMD CasesPM2.5PM10SO2NO2COO3Average temperatureAtmospheric pressureRelative humidityWind speedHFMD Cases1.00***PM2.5−0.23***1.00***PM10−0.20***0.96***1.00***SO20.08***0.60***0.60***1.00***NO2−0.06***0.65***0.63***0.67***1.00***CO−0.10***0.61***0.53***0.54***0.702***1.00***O3−0.0160.60***0.64***0.32***0.23***0.17***1.00***Mean temperature0.61***−0.46***−0.41***−0.09***−0.29***−0.35***−0.04*1.00***Atmospheric pressure−0.57***0.51***0.50***0.17***0.24***0.28***0.18***−0.85***1.00***Relative humidity0.20***−0.44***−0.54***−0.40***−0.11***−0.12***−0.52***0.23***−0.48***1.00***Wind speed0.12***−0.01−0.010.12***−0.08***0.14***−0.09***−0.09***0.04*−0.15***1.00****p < 0.05; ***p < 0.001.Distributed lag nonlinear modelsWe used 3-D plots and contour graphs to depict the non-linear, lagged exposure-response for air pollution and meteorological variables (Figures 3, 4). SO2 and CO showed associations with HFMD at high concentrations with SO2 showing delay effect and CO showing instant effect. At low concentrations, both NO2 and O3 were associated with higher HFMD risks, where NO2 presents an immediate lag risk and O3 has a delayed lag risk. When concentrations are high, NO2 still retains its immediate harmful effect, while increased O3-related risk can be detected after longer lag periods. Overall, PM2.5 and PM10 appeared to have a protective effect at high concentration levels. Mean temperature, relative humidity, and wind speed exhibited biphasic exposure–response relationships with HFMD, and the correlation was more marked for low levels of temperature and high levels of wind speed and relative humidity. Atmospheric pressure presented a significant relationship with HFMD at high exposure levels.Figure 33-D plot and contour of RR along air pollution variables and lags.Diagram consists of six 3D surface plots and six corresponding contour plots in two rows, each relating air pollutant concentration and lag period to relative risk; pollutants shown are SO2, NO2, CO, O3, PM2.5, and PM10. In contrast, NO2 showed a decreasing trend. HFMD-related risk increased with relative humidity, with high humidity corresponding to elevated incidence risk. PM2.5 and PM10 showed similar patterns, with peaks at low concentrations and protective effects at higher concentrations. Notably, O3 and mean temperature both presented dual-risk peaks. O3 reached risk peaks at 74.5 μg/m3 (RR = 1.17, 95% CI: 1.13–1.20) and 316.0 μg/m3 (RR = 1.15, 95% CI: 0.71–1.84); temperature had two peaks at 3.5 °C (RR = 6.67, 95% CI: 3.45–12.73) and 33.0 °C (RR = 3.43, 95% CI: 2.85–4.14).Figure 5Cumulative effects of air pollution factors on HFMD incidence within 21 days.Six line graphs display the overall cumulative association between six air pollutants (SO2, NO2, CO, O3, PM2.5, PM10) and relative risk from 0 to 21 days. full_text_sections.abstract: AbstractBackgroundIn China, hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) persists as a prevalent infectious disease with high transmissibility. Nevertheless, the link between environmental determinants and HFMD incidence has not been fully elucidated. The study assessed associations between air pollution, meteorological conditions, and HFMD incidence in Shenzhen, China, while also evaluating shifts in these associations before and after the Enterovirus 71 vaccine and during the COVID-19 epidemic.MethodsDaily data on HFMD cases, air pollutants (such as PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NO2, CO, and O3), and meteorological variables (including mean temperature, relative humidity, atmospheric pressure, and wind speed) were collected for the period from 2013 to 2022. Associations were assessed using distributed lag non-linear models (DLNM), accounting for immediate and delayed effects.ResultsSpearman correlation analysis showed that HFMD was positively correlated with SO2, mean temperature, relative humidity, and wind speed, and negatively with PM2.5, PM10, NO2, CO, and atmospheric pressure. DLNM models revealed that SO2 and CO both elevated cumulative risk at extremely high concentrations, with SO2 showing delayed effects. However, SO2 unexpectedly displayed protective effects in single-lag analysis. NO2 exhibited a U-shaped risk at extreme concentrations despite an overall decreasing trend. O3 showed dual peaks, with protective effects at extremely high concentrations after lag 1. PM2.5 and PM10 showed risk peaks at low concentrations but protective effects at extremely high concentrations. Temperature exhibited a dual-peak risk pattern at extremely low and extremely high temperatures, with extreme heat producing sustained effects and extreme cold shorter-lived risk. HFMD risk increased under conditions of extremely high humidity. In general, the risk associated with atmospheric pressure rose as pressure levels increased, and asymmetric lagged effects were observed at both low- and high-concentration extremes. Extremely high wind speed causing short-term harm and extremely low wind speed leading to delayed cumulative risk.ConclusionMeteorological factors exhibit more consistent associations than air pollutants. Mean temperature showed a dual-peak distribution with persistent effects from high temperatures, while atmospheric pressure presented long-lasting impacts of low pressure. There is a positive correlation between relative humidity and the incidence of HFMD. Air pollutants showed inconsistent associations with HFMD. These findings support targeted public health interventions for meteorological factors.Keywords: air pollution, DLNM, effect, HFMD, meteorological variables
full_text_sections.methods: MethodsResearch area descriptionShenzhen, situated in the southern part of Guangdong Province, is a coastal metropolis sharing its border with Hong Kong and Macao. The city extends over 1,997 square kilometers and falls within the subtropical monsoon climate zone, experiencing an average annual temperature of nearly 23 °C. Over the 2013–2022 study period, Shenzhen’s annual permanent resident population stood between 12.57 million and 17.66 million, recording an average population of around 15.75 million.1 Geographically, Shenzhen lies within the coordinates 113.43°–114.38° E and 22.24°–22.52° N.2Data collectionDaily reported cases of HFMD covering the period 2013 to 2022 were collected from the infectious disease surveillance networks of Shenzhen Center for Disease Control and Prevention. Daily data spanning the same period, which included daily concentrations of air pollutants (PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NO2, CO, and O3) as well as meteorological conditions (mean temperature, relative humidity, atmospheric pressure, and wind speed), were acquired from Shenzhen Ecological Environment Monitoring Center Station and Meteorological Bureau of Shenzhen Municipality.3Statistical analysesDescriptive statistics summarized HFMD and environmental variables. To evaluate the associations between HFMD incidence and air pollution as well as meteorological factors, Spearman correlation analysis was conducted. The Spearman correlation coefficient was calculated as:rs=1−6∑i=1ndi2n(n2−1)Where di represents the difference between the ranks of paired observations for the i-th pair, and n is the number of observations. The Spearman coefficient ranges from −1 to +1, with positive values indicating a positive monotonic association and negative values indicating an inverse association. Statistical significance was defined as a two-sided p-value < 0.05.In line with earlier research, a quasi-Poisson regression framework incorporating distributed lag nonlinear models (DLNM) was used to examine the associations between air pollutants and meteorological conditions on HFMD occurrence, taking into account data distribution characteristics and inter-variable relationships. The model is specified as follows:log[E(Yt)]=α+cb(X,df=3,lag=21)+ns(Time,df=6/year)+Σns(Xi,df=3)+βDOWt+γHOLIDAYt+δVACt+εCOVtWhere α represents the intercept, and Yt is the number of HFMD cases observed on day t. The term cb(·) denotes the cross-basis function constructed with 3 df for the exposure dimension (natural cubic splines with knots placed at the 33rd and 67th percentiles) and 3 df for the lag dimension (natural cubic splines), with a maximum lag of 21 days. Each of the 10 environmental variables — PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NO2, CO, O3, mean temperature, relative humidity, atmospheric pressure, and wind speed — was separately examined as the primary exposure.For each model, natural cubic spline functions ns(·) with 3 df were applied to the remaining environmental variables (Xi) to adjust for their potential confounding effects. Given the high collinearity between PM2.5 and PM10 [Spearman ρ > 0.85; variance inflation factor (VIF) > 5; Supplementary Table S4], these two particulate matter fractions were not included simultaneously in any model. Specifically, when a meteorological variable (temperature, relative humidity, atmospheric pressure, or wind speed) served as the primary exposure, the covariates comprised the remaining meteorological variables together with CO, SO2, NO2, O3, and PM2.5 (PM10 excluded). When CO, SO2, NO2, or O3 served as the primary exposure, the covariates comprised the other three gaseous pollutants, all four meteorological variables, and PM2.5 (PM10 excluded). When PM2.5 or PM10 served as the primary exposure, the covariates comprised all four meteorological variables and the four gaseous pollutants (CO, SO2, NO2, O3), with the alternate particulate matter fraction excluded.The Time variable was specified with 6 df per year to capture long-term temporal trends and seasonal patterns, selected based on the quasi-Akaike information criterion (QAIC) (Supplementary Table S1). DOW and HOLIDAY denote the effects of the day of the week and public holidays. VAC and COV indicate whether the date fell within the EV71 vaccination or COVID-19 prevention period. Knot placement at the 33rd and 67th percentiles was selected based on QAIC comparison with alternative strategies (Supplementary Table S3). Cumulative RRs at the 95th percentile were compared between the full-period (2013–2022) and pre-pandemic (2013–2019) datasets (Supplementary Table S5). The effects of extreme exposures were expressed as relative risks (RRs), comparing the 5th and 95th percentiles to the median.Table 1Descriptive study of HFMD and environmental factors.VariablesMean ± SDMin25th50th75thMaxNumber of cases/day130 ± 14401777204885PM2.5 (μg/m3)26.34 ± 17.232.3313.7322.5534.86136.52PM10 (μg/m3)44.1 ± 24.883.2026.0438.1856.28179.77SO2 (μg/m3)7.73 ± 3.553.095.536.808.8256.03NO2 (μg/m3)32.06 ± 15.874.4021.2528.8938.77139.53CO (mg/m3)0.78 ± 0.260.390.570.710.901.92O3 (μg/m3)102.72 ± 45.7519.1866.7094.62128.38316.27Mean temperature(。C)23.62 ± 5.343.519.624.7528.233Atmospheric pressure (hPa)1005.63 ± 6.34983.11000.81005.61010.51027.3Relative humidity (%)75.41 ± 12.6819707884100Wind speed (m/s)1.83 ± 0.770.31.31.72.26.1To evaluate the potential influence of residual autocorrelation on our estimates, we performed the following two-step sensitivity analysis. First, the Pearson residuals of each main DLNM model were extracted, and residual autocorrelation was assessed diagnostically using the autocorrelation function (ACF) and the Ljung–Box test at lags of 10 and 20 days (Supplementary Table S6; Supplementary Figure S1). Second, to explicitly adjust for the first-order residual autocorrelation identified in the first step, we re-fitted each model including the first-order lagged Pearson residual as an additional covariate (hereinafter the AR(1)-adjusted model). full_text_sections.discussion: DiscussionClimate change and urbanization have significantly transformed environmental conditions, such as air quality, temperature, and relative humidity, potentially influencing the spread of infectious diseases, including HFMD, dengue fever, Chikungunya fever, malaria, and COVID-19 (25–28). HFMD remains a key public health issue, especially among children. Understanding how air pollution and meteorological variables impact HFMD is crucial to developing targeted prevention and intervention measures. A DLNM was applied in this study to examine the relationships between air pollutants, meteorological factors, and the incidence of HFMD, accounting for week, holidays, EV71 vaccination, and COVID-19 periods.We observed SO2 and CO both presented elevated cumulative risks when their concentrations were at higher levels, even though the effects observed at specific lag days were complicated. High-concentration SO2 showed a delayed cumulative risk, which is consistent with the results reported in earlier studies (17, 29). However, it unexpectedly displayed protective effects in single-lag analysis. This discrepancy is most likely caused by the non-linear U-shaped relationship, which is characterized differently in different time dimensions. Although the mechanism by which SO2 affects HFMD incidence remains unclear, it’s well-documented that SO2 could disturb the balance of the regular intestinal microflora, which may affect the development of children’s immune systems (30). CO showed a negative Spearman correlation but increasing cumulative risk at high concentrations, with the discrepancy attributable to Spearman’s inability to capture U-shaped non-linearity. The results from Tang and Yan’s research (12, 22) also suggest that extremely high levels of CO elevate the risk of HFMD. However, the underlying mechanisms linking CO to HFMD are not well understood and warrant future investigation. NO2 displayed a decreasing cumulative trend but U-shaped risk at extreme concentrations, with delayed-increasing harmful effects at high levels. Inconsistencies with findings in other studies (17, 31, 32) highlight the need for multi-city analyses. O3, a byproduct of NOx (33), exhibited different effects from NO2 on HFMD incidence. O3 presented dual cumulative peaks at 74.5 μg/m3 (RR = 1.17) and 316.0 μg/m3 (RR = 1.15, 95% CI: 0.71–1.84). High O3 concentrations exerted protective effects after lag 1. This result is incompatible with most current studies, which found that O3 concentration is positively correlated with HFMD incidence (12, 17, 34). However, in Yu’s study (15) elevated O3 concentrations had a mild protective influence on HFMD. Their inference suggests that O3 may affect infectious diseases, likely through inhibition of the persistence and reproduction of bacteria and viruses in ambient environments. PM2.5 and PM10, highly collinear (r = 0.96) and modeled separately, showed risk peaks at low concentrations followed by protective effects at high concentrations, consistent with inverted V-shaped curves and protective effects in Sichuan (13). During periods of high PM2.5 and PM10 concentrations, residents may modify their-related behaviors, which could reduce the risk of HFMD infection. Specifically, reduced outdoor activity time (35, 36) and increased mask-wearing on heavily polluted days (37) may partly explain this protective association.Our study also found that mean temperature had the strongest correlation with HFMD (r = 0.61), and we observed a dual-peak cumulative risk pattern at both low (3.5 °C, RR = 6.67) and high (33.0 °C, RR = 3.43) temperatures. Dual peaks were also found in studies of Tianjin, Ningbo and Shijiazhuang (14, 34, 38). Elevated temperatures may exacerbate viral proliferation and boost human outdoor activities, such as summer camps,thereby facilitating virus transmission (39, 40). On colder days, human immune function might be compromised. Brief exposure to low temperatures could shorten the incubation period of microbes, leading to a higher incidence of infections (40, 41). Lagged analysis revealed asymmetric dynamics: extreme heat maintained sustained harmful effects over lag 0–21 days, whereas extreme cold produced shorter-lived risk at lag 1–2 days, suggesting that heat-related risk requires longer forecast windows. Relative humidity was positively associated with HFMD, with risk increasing monotonically — consistent with other findings (11, 22, 40, 42). Studies have demonstrated that high humidity may extend viral persistence (43). Conversely, the protective effect of low humidity aligns with accelerated viral inactivation under dry conditions, where desiccation causes structural damage to the viral capsid (44). Atmospheric pressure showed the second strongest correlation (r = −0.57), with cumulative risk increasing at higher pressure — consistent with Zhu et al. (42) and Sun et al. (45). The lagged analysis revealed a notably asymmetric pattern: high pressure produced short-term harmful effects, possibly reflecting behavioral changes during fair-weather conditions, while low pressure led to gradually increasing risk that persisted. The extended lag window provides significant lead time for early warning. Wind speed was positively correlated with HFMD, consistent with Guangzhou (46) and Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei (47). Our lagged analysis showed a biphasic pattern: high wind speed caused short-term harmful effects (lag 1–2) indicating that higher wind speeds may enhance airborne transmission of the virus in densely populated areas (42, 48). While low wind speed produced gradually increasing risk, possibly through facilitating the occurrence of bioaerosols (49).Notably, the study period spanned both pre- and post-COVID-19 pandemic phases, and the temporal pattern of HFMD incidence shifted markedly after 2020. To test whether pandemic-era alterations in healthcare-seeking behavior and non-pharmaceutical interventions distorted the environmental exposure–HFMD associations, we conducted subgroup sensitivity analyses stratified by pandemic period. The effects of extreme high and low levels of meteorological factors remained broadly consistent in direction and significance across the two periods, supporting the robustness of the meteorological findings. For air pollutants, the effects of high-concentration exposure—the primary concern in air pollution health research—were likewise maintained in direction and significance across the two periods, indicating that the high-exposure findings are robust to the exclusion of the pandemic period. By contrast, several low-concentration associations (e.g., PM2.5, PM10, and O3) were sensitive to the exclusion of the pandemic period: when the analysis was restricted to 2013–2019, these associations changed from protective to risk-increasing in direction. This directional instability suggests that the estimated effects at the lower concentration range are not robust and may reflect, at least in part, the sparse data at low exposure levels, the relatively short post-pandemic observation period, and pandemic-related changes in exposure distributions and healthcare-seeking behavior. Accordingly, the low-concentration findings for PM2.5, PM10, and O3 should be interpreted with caution and regarded as exploratory. Taken together, our results suggest that the main conclusions, which are driven primarily by associations at high exposure levels, were not substantially biased by pandemic-related changes; however, the low-concentration associations identified in the full-period analysis warrant more cautious interpretation, and residual confounding by unmeasured or time-varying factors could not be fully excluded.In the present study, the impacts of air pollutants and meteorological factors on HFMD incidence were investigated, encompassing the pre- and post-EV71 vaccination periods as well as the COVID-19 control period. Notably, our research findings offer practical guidance in two key dimensions. Firstly, our re…
full_text_sections.conclusion: ConclusionThis study used DLNM models to investigate non-linear and lagged associations between meteorological factors, air pollutants and HFMD incidence. Meteorological factors — particularly mean temperature and atmospheric pressure — serve as the primary environmental drivers of HFMD, exhibiting more consistent associations than air pollutants. Mean temperature showed a dual-peak distribution with persistent effects from high temperatures, while atmospheric pressure presented long-lasting impacts of low pressure. There is a positive correlation between relative humidity and the incidence of HFMD. Air pollutants showed inconsistent associations with HFMD. The seemingly protective effect of PM at high concentrations was probably not real, but rather a result of confounding by other factors. These findings support targeted interventions during extreme temperature, high humidity, and sustained low-pressure periods.
